name: Buffer
tagline: Social media scheduler for publishing posts across channels

pricing.notes: Official pricing/help checked 2026-07-30; Essentials listed at $6/channel/month monthly and $5/channel/month annually.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 3 channels; 10 scheduled posts/channel; 100 ideas; 1 user; 1 API key; 3,000 API requests/month; 5 AI reply suggestions/week; 1 saved reply; 30-day analytics history.

tiers.name: Essentials
tiers.limits: Per connected channel; up to 5,000 queued posts/channel under fair use; 1 user; 3 API keys; 7,500 API requests/month.
tiers.notes: Every paid channel is charged, including the first 3.

tiers.name: Team
tiers.limits: Per connected channel; up to 5,000 queued posts/channel under fair use; unlimited users; 5 API keys; 15,000 API requests/month.
tiers.notes: Every paid channel is charged, including the first 3.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 3 channels; 10 scheduled posts/channel; 100 ideas; 1 user; 1 API key; 3,000 API requests/month; 5 AI reply suggestions/week; 1 saved reply; 30-day analytics history
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (2 months free); 14-day no-card trial, then auto-downgrades to Free if not upgraded
pricing.hiddenCosts: Pricing is per connected channel, and a Start Page counts as a channel. Volume discounts begin after 10 channels, but the full current discount schedule is not publicly itemized.

verdictSummary: Posting to one or two APIs is easy, but maintaining social platform auth, queues, previews, analytics, and API-policy compliance is real ongoing work.
coreLoopDIY: Create a post queue, connect one social API, schedule jobs, publish posts, and log outcomes.
requirements: OAuth/API access for each social network
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because social APIs break and scheduling must be reliable.

priorArt.name: Postiz
priorArt.desc: Open-source social media scheduling tool and strong Buffer-like prior art.

alternatives.name: Adobe Express Free
alternatives.desc: Six networks, a visual editor and a thousand scheduled posts a month; analytics and team workflow are not invited.

facts.install: Hosted web signup or Adobe Express mobile app
facts.engines: Adobe Firefly powers generative text and image features; Adobe does not publish a complete backend-model list.
facts.dataFormat: Designs, media, drafts, and scheduled-post metadata live in Adobe's cloud; connected social networks receive the published content, and the internal storage format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: It does not replace Buffer's dedicated community inbox or channel-focused advanced analytics, so engagement and performance review remain shallower.
facts.setupBlocker: Each social profile needs OAuth authorization, and Adobe says scheduler connections expire after 60 days and must be reconnected.

alternatives.name: BrightBean Studio
alternatives.desc: A startlingly complete free scheduler: approvals, inbox, analytics, clients, API and MCP, with someone else running the servers.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or Docker Compose for self-hosting
facts.dataFormat: The hosted service stores application data in BrightBean's infrastructure; self-hosting uses PostgreSQL for application data and server-controlled storage for media, while local development can use SQLite.
facts.gapVsPaid: Its biggest weakness is maturity: a much smaller project and hosted service have less established platform-change coverage and support history than Buffer.
facts.setupBlocker: The hosted version is straightforward; self-hosting needs Docker, a public domain, and developer credentials or OAuth apps for the social networks.

alternatives.name: Buffer Free
alternatives.desc: Three channels, ten queued posts each and thirty days of metrics; eight lifetime channel connections make swapping a one-way door.

facts.engines: Buffer AI Assistant; Buffer does not disclose the underlying model provider on its pricing page.
facts.dataFormat: Posts, drafts, ideas, analytics, and connected-account metadata live in Buffer's cloud; the internal storage format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: The free plan cuts the working queue to 10 scheduled posts per channel, removes advanced analytics, and permanently counts each of the first eight unique channel connections.

alternatives.name: Fedica Free
alternatives.desc: Ten network accounts and ten queued posts total, refilling forever; generous until you plan eleven things at once.

facts.dataFormat: Queued posts, account connections, and analytics live in Fedica's cloud; the internal storage format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: Fedica permits only 10 live scheduled posts across the whole free account and only one account per platform, a much tighter working queue than paid Buffer.

alternatives.name: Mixpost Lite
alternatives.desc: A polished single-user scheduler with queues and basic analytics; the serious team features live in the paid edition.

facts.install: Docker Compose; manual Laravel installation is also documented
facts.dataFormat: Application data lives in MySQL or MariaDB, queues and cache in Redis, and media on local disk or configured S3-compatible storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Mixpost Lite replaces Buffer's managed service with a server you must secure, back up, update, and keep connected to changing social APIs.
facts.setupBlocker: A non-expert needs a server, Docker, a domain with TLS, cron/queue workers, and social-platform application credentials.

alternatives.name: Postiz
alternatives.desc: The broadest open scheduler here; free means running PostgreSQL, Redis, Temporal and your own platform credentials.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or the official Docker Compose stack
facts.dataFormat: Self-hosted data spans PostgreSQL, Redis, and Temporal; uploads use local persistent storage or configured object storage such as Cloudflare R2. Hosted data lives in Postiz's cloud.
facts.gapVsPaid: The software is broad, but self-hosting its PostgreSQL, Redis, Temporal, storage, and OAuth stack is far more operational work than paying Buffer.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting is a substantial stack: the docs call for PostgreSQL, Redis, Temporal, persistent storage, a public domain, and each network's OAuth credentials, with 4 vCPU and 8 GB RAM recommended.

alternatives.name: Publer Free
alternatives.desc: Three non-X accounts and ten queued posts each; yesterday's history disappears tomorrow.

facts.dataFormat: Posts, media, drafts, history, and connected-account metadata live in Publer's cloud; the internal storage format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: The free plan excludes X and retains published-post history for only 24 hours, which makes meaningful review and reuse markedly worse than Buffer.

alternatives.name: Social Champ Free
alternatives.desc: Three non-X accounts, fifteen queued posts each, analytics and an inbox; one user and no X publishing.

facts.engines: Champ AI Suite; Social Champ does not identify the underlying model provider on its pricing page.
facts.dataFormat: Posts, media, analytics, inbox messages, and connected-account metadata live in Social Champ's cloud; the internal storage format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: The free plan excludes X and limits the queue to 15 posts per account, while Buffer's paid plan supports X and effectively removes the queue ceiling.

notes: Great social example: one channel is easy; social-platform maintenance is not.
prompt:
Build me a personal social post scheduler to replace Buffer. Requirements:

- Node + Express + better-sqlite3; a localhost page with a compose box,
  image attach, and the queue ordered by send time.
- Two targets only: Mastodon (access token) and Bluesky (app password via
  @atproto/api), creds in .env. One small adapter file per network so a
  third is addable later, but scaffold nothing I don't use.
- Buffer-style slots: I define posting times (say weekdays 09:00 and 17:00
  in my timezone) and new posts fill the next free slot; a post can also be
  pinned to an exact datetime.
- A node-cron tick every minute publishes due posts, marks each row sent or
  failed, retries failures 3 times with backoff, and marks before sending so
  nothing ever double-posts.
- Per-network character counter in the composer; attached images stored in
  media/ next to the database.
- A history page of the last 100 sent posts linking to the live posts.
- Runs on my always-on box; localhost only, no accounts, no telemetry.
- Out of scope: X, Instagram, and LinkedIn (paid, approval-gated, or hostile
  APIs, say so in the README), analytics, and rich post previews.
- README: getting a Mastodon access token and a Bluesky app password.
